newsitem.title: OMAN: Oman, India to build fertiliser plant in September.
newsitem.headline: Oman, India to build fertiliser plant in September.

text.p: Construction work on a $1.0 billion joint Omani-Indian fertiliser plant is due to start in Oman in September, Commerce and Industry Minister Makboul Bin Ali Bin Sultan was quoted as saying on Tuesday.
"Work will start in September," he told the Oman newspaper.
State-owned Oman Oil Co and India's Krishak Bharati Cooperative Ltd (KRIBHCO) and Rashtriya Chemicals and Fertilisers Limited are behind the project due to start production by the year 2000.
Omani and India government officials finalised the project in August last year. Oman Oil Co holds 50 percent equity while the Indian partners each hold 25 percent.
Bin Sultan did not disclose who had been awarded the contracts for the construction work.
He told the newspaper that Oman and the Indian partners were each putting up $300 million of the cost while the rest would be raised through loans.
The plant, to be built at Sur, southeast of the capital Muscat, will export 1.45 million tonnes of urea a year to India.
